## Plan document present and linked

Pass. The required plan exists at [dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:1), is substantive, and is linked as a `design` document in the planning issue at [.jit/issues/e131f1dc-c5a9-41eb-a6e4-ee9e1d5ba57f.json](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/.jit/issues/e131f1dc-c5a9-41eb-a6e4-ee9e1d5ba57f.json:117). The linked investigation and research documents are also present and complete.

## Completeness against the criteria

The plan explicitly maps all eleven `[hard]` container criteria in §1 and provides concrete implementation leaves and acceptance checks in §3. It preserves the CLI/server/web/MCP scope, covers all three audit domains, release identity, artifact publication, Docker consolidation, documentation ownership, MSRV policy, rehearsal, and external core/profile integration.

REQ-11 is textually covered but not executable as currently wired: the source-freeze leaf requires the external core-maintenance epic itself to become terminal, contradicting that epic’s standing lifecycle decision. This is blocking and detailed below.

## Technical soundness and architectural fit

The local architectural claims are accurate:

- The server validates and watches an existing `.jit` directory and derives repository context from its parent in [crates/server/src/main.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/crates/server/src/main.rs:61).
- API routing, embedded-web fallback, and the current lack of graceful shutdown match [crates/server/src/main.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/crates/server/src/main.rs:104).
- The existing Docker image builds Rust before the web bundle and uses nginx, Node, root execution, `/data`, and a shell supervisor, as described in [Dockerfile](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/Dockerfile:20) and [docker/entrypoint.sh](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/docker/entrypoint.sh:12).
- The hosted-service assumptions are also current: npm supports stage-only trusted publishers bound to a GitHub environment and requires human 2FA approval of a stage ([npm trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/), [npm staged publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/staged-publishing/)); GitHub immutable releases lock assets and the associated tag after publishing ([GitHub immutable releases](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/immutable-releases)); Rust 1.97 is current ([Rust 1.97 announcement](https://blog.rust-lang.org/releases/latest/)).

The only advisory technical defect is the unexplained “binding D-14” reference in §Decisions: no D-14 exists in the charter, issue description, or repository search.

## Decomposition and dependencies

Most of the decomposition is coherent:

- Remediation precedes blocking security enforcement.
- Graceful server shutdown precedes the consolidated image, which precedes topology removal.
- Source-changing work converges before source freeze.
- Candidate production, assembly, staging, rehearsal, final tagging, and publication are correctly ordered.
- The MCP execution leaf now explicitly depends on the native/source candidate producer at [plan line 277](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:277).

However, “Freeze the exact integrated v1.0 source” depends directly on `6eb585bc` and requires both external epics to be terminal at [plan lines 242–245](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:242). Core maintenance is expressly an open living container, and its current handoff says it remains open after every child resolves at [dev/active/6eb585bc-handoff.md line 33](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/6eb585bc-handoff.md:33). JIT considers only `Done` and `Rejected` dependencies met, as documented in [containment-and-completion.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/docs/concepts/containment-and-completion.md:76). Consequently, the freeze and every downstream release leaf remain blocked indefinitely. The plan needs a terminal v1 core-maintenance checkpoint or an explicitly approved change to the living-container decision.

## Risks and actionability

The plan is otherwise unusually actionable: leaves have bounded blast radii, observable criteria, explicit ownership, and meaningful failure tests.

The risk entry at plan line 382 claims the direct core-epic dependency mitigates late contract changes, but it does not address the epic’s non-terminal lifecycle. That is a load-bearing unresolved risk, not an implementation detail.

## Prior review feedback

Both prior blocking findings are resolved:

- Prior F1: the MCP candidate now depends on and consumes the retained native candidate at plan lines 277–281.
- Prior F2: bootstrap now creates a distinct protected, candidate-ref-restricted, secret-free `npm-stage` environment at lines 93–95; staging tooling declares `environment: npm-stage` and minimal permissions at line 165; the actual stage leaf repeats that contract at lines 304–307.

## Findings

1. **F1 — High, blocking:** The source-freeze leaf depends on the terminal state of `6eb585bc`, but core maintenance has a standing decision to remain open as a living container after all children resolve. Because non-terminal dependencies remain unmet, the release DAG cannot reach source freeze, rehearsal, or publication. Replace the dependency with a terminal v1 core checkpoint or obtain and record an explicit decision to close/reject the living epic.

2. **F2 — Low, advisory:** Plan decision D9 calls its external-dependency choice “binding D-14,” but no D-14 exists in the charter, relevant issues, or repository. Link the actual decision source or remove the stale attribution.

Total findings: 2
